cases.obligation: A callback event carrying this process instance marker is ignored before normalized input accounting or queue insertion.
A physical or external callback event carrying a different marker continues through the normalized input queue.
The process marker is created and copied into callback state before tap installation and into the executor worker.
Every generated keyboard event receives the process marker before it is posted.
A keyboard action generates key-down events in configured order and key-up events in reverse order.
Unavailable post-event access fails before any event generation or injection.
A NULL event creation releases only already-owned events and posts no partial keyboard chord.
A later repeat generation failure is classified after injection once an earlier repeat was posted.
Keys without an unambiguous current macOS virtual-key mapping are rejected before event generation.
The action mailbox has fixed capacity, preserves accepted FIFO order, and drops a new action on overload.
A stopped action worker rejects new work without blocking the input owner.
Executor shutdown remains bounded when an in-flight OS leaf does not return.
The production input step evaluates context need, conditionally observes and reads context, then invokes the existing consumer in that order.
Production context observation is inactive for disabled or bindingless configuration and submits mouse movement or only a button-down with a relevant binding.
Fresh matched context selects and dispatches the existing ordered macOS keyboard action.
Unknown or stale context never dispatches a macOS action.

A context-not-needed transition records a monotonic request-id boundary, so a same-tick pre-transition completion is rejected and only a later request id can restore context while point and tick freshness checks remain required.
